service.name: Corporate retreat entertainment in Aspen
service.serviceType: Live music for corporate retreats and incentive events
service.description: Live music for corporate retreats and private celebrations at Aspen venues, solo through quartet, with travel and lodging published as their own lines.

faqs.q: What does live music cost in Aspen?
faqs.a: Three published lines: the resort column of the rate card for the size you book, a flat $600 travel line, and lodging billed at cost. Sound sized to the venue is included at every size. The arithmetic, set against the wider Colorado market, is worked through in our cost guide.

faqs.q: Why is lodging on an Aspen quote?
faqs.a: Because an Aspen date is a two-day commitment. The drive runs about four hours in good conditions and longer in winter, and a band that finishes at eleven is not driving mountain highways home that night. Lodging bills at what it costs, on its own line, never marked up.

faqs.q: How long is the drive from Denver, really?
faqs.a: About four hours when the roads cooperate. Independence Pass closes seasonally, so winter dates run the long way through Glenwood Springs, and weather can stretch any of it. We build that margin into the load-in day rather than into your evening.

faqs.q: Can the party run outdoors in Aspen?
faqs.a: Until eight. Outdoor amplified sound at a private event was reported capped at 80 dBA at the perimeter, between 9am and 8pm, when we checked, with neighbours within 250 feet owed seven days' notice. Evenings move indoors from there, and we confirm the current figures with your venue.

faqs.q: What size fits an Aspen dinner?
faqs.a: A duo or a trio holding 65 to 72 dBA at the nearest table is the working answer for dinner at The Little Nell or Hotel Jerome class of venue. A quartet is the booking when a dance floor is the objective, and the quartet is our published ceiling for 2026.
